turns.query: Regarding our previous machine purchase, can we claim capital allowances if we sold the old machine, but we subsequently purchased another machine for SGD 100,000?
turns.answer:
# Answer

Accounting depreciation is disallowed for tax, and in its place, Capital Allowances are granted on qualifying plant and machinery used in trade or business.

A capital allowance claim made under Section 19A(1) can be deferred and does not need to be claimed consecutively over 3 YAs. [IRAS: IRAS | Capital Allowances](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/capital-allowances)

When a fixed asset is sold, converted to trading stock or written off, you need to calculate balancing allowance or balancing charge if capital allowances have been claimed on the cost of the asset previously. [IRAS: IRAS | Capital Allowances](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/capital-allowances)

Show your basis of calculating the total capital allowance claimed, giving a breakdown of the cost/ tax written down value brought forward, capital allowance amount and tax written down value carried forward for each category of assets. [IRAS: IRAS | Capital Allowances](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/capital-allowances)

turns.query: Our employee is covered by the Employment Act and the overtime provisions. Do ordinary salary and overtime have the same payment deadline after the salary period ends? Explain the practical payroll steps and cite the relevant official guidance. No journal is required.
turns.answer:
# Answer

Salary must be paid:

• Within 7 days after the end of the salary period

• For overtime work, within 14 days after the end of the salary period [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

In accordance with the Employment Act and Ministry of Manpower official guidance, ordinary salary must be paid within 7 days after the end of the salary period. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Employers must issue itemised pay slips and keep detailed employment and salary records for employees covered by the Employment Act. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

turns.query: Does that change if the employee is not covered by the overtime provisions? Please keep ordinary salary and overtime separate. No journal is required.
turns.answer:
# Answer

According to the Ministry of Manpower, employers must pay ordinary salary at least once a month and within 7 days after the end of the salary period, regardless of whether the employee is covered by overtime provisions. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

If an employee is not covered by Part 4 of the Employment Act and its overtime provisions, the employee is not entitled to statutory overtime pay under those provisions, and terms regarding hours of work and any additional compensation are determined by the employment contract. [MOM: Hours of work, overtime and rest day](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days)

If you are not covered under Part 4 of the Employment Act, your terms and conditions of employment will be according to your employment contract. [MOM: Hours of work, overtime and rest day](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/hours-of-work-overtime-and-rest-days)
